With its expert cast firing on all cylinders, the Pulitzer Prize-nominated Becky Shaw sends laughter rocketing throughout the audience with its scathing portrayal of social mores being blown to smithereens.

That theatergoers are unlikely to wind up dismissing any of these blunt-speaking characters as complete boors is a testament to the playwright’s rich, nuanced writing, and the layered portrayals by the stellar five-member cast, three of whom are making impressive Broadway debuts.

It’s a bracingly intelligent and deeply engaging work, one that justifies its long journey to Broadway by reminding us of the theater’s unique capacity to hold a mirror up to our most intimate—and most unsettling—selves.

cn.t: Gionfriddo's razor-sharp dark comedy wins raves for its brutally honest dissection of toxic relationships and class dynamics. Critics hail the "hilariously ruthless" dialogue and stellar cast, though a few find the caustic characters off-putting.

vr.q: Becky Shaw is the kind of play that'll make you laugh, gasp, and question, who is in the right here? And then realise the answer is maybe no one. And that's what makes it so compelling.
The emotional manipulation, the ruthlessness, and the downright cruelty would be completely unappetizing if it weren't so damn funny.
It's a play where the craft is more impressive than the emotional payoff.
